parts.zh: M：今天我们的嘉宾是 Rosie Mullender
W：我们每天都会查看记者们的创意
M：在工作日里，你通常会做哪些工作？
W：我的一天主要包括回复电子邮件
M：专题编辑的工作与时尚编辑或其他编辑职位有什么不同？
W：专题编辑团队负责职业
M：很多人认为，在杂志社工作是一份光鲜亮丽的工作
W：我会说这份工作在一定程度上确实很光鲜
M：为了在事业上走到今天这一步
W：那你应该看看。它也非常有趣

items.stem: What is the woman's profession?

choices.text: Magazine reporter
choices.zh: 杂志记者

choices.text: Fashion designer
choices.zh: 时装设计师

choices.text: Website designer
choices.zh: 网站设计师

choices.text: Features editor
choices.zh: 专题编辑

items.stem: What is one of the woman's main responsibilities?

choices.text: Designing sports clothing
choices.zh: 设计运动服装

choices.text: Consulting fashion experts
choices.zh: 咨询时尚专家

choices.text: Answering daily emails
choices.zh: 回复日常邮件

choices.text: Interviewing job-seekers
choices.zh: 面试求职者

items.stem: What do many people think about the woman's job?

choices.text: It is challenging.
choices.zh: 具有挑战性

choices.text: It is fascinating.
choices.zh: 令人着迷

choices.text: It is tiresome.
choices.zh: 令人厌烦

choices.text: It is fashionable.
choices.zh: 时尚

items.stem: What helped the woman to get her current position?

choices.text: Her persistence
choices.zh: 她的坚持不懈

choices.text: Her experience
choices.zh: 她的经验

choices.text: Her competence
choices.zh: 她的能力

choices.text: Her confidence
choices.zh: 她的自信

items.stem: What does the man think of the satire Frankie he recently watched?

choices.text: It is enjoyable.
choices.zh: 它很有趣。

choices.text: It is educational.
choices.zh: 它很有教育意义。

choices.text: It is divorced from real life.
choices.zh: 它脱离现实生活。

choices.text: It is adapted from a drama.
choices.zh: 它改编自一部戏剧。

items.stem: What does the man say is special about the satire Frankie?

choices.text: All the roles are played by famous actors and actresses.
choices.zh: 所有角色都由著名演员出演。

choices.text: It is based on the real-life experiences of some celebrities.
choices.zh: 它根据一些名人的真实生活经历改编。

choices.text: Its plots and events reveal a lot about Frankie's actual life.
choices.zh: 它的情节和事件揭示了很多 Frankie 的真实生活。

choices.text: It is written, directed, edited and produced by Frankie himself
choices.zh: 它由 Frankie 本人编剧、导演、剪辑和制作。

items.stem: What does the woman say she is going to do with the satire Frankie?

choices.text: Go to the theater and enjoy it.
choices.zh: 去影院观看它。

choices.text: Recommend it to her friends.
choices.zh: 把它推荐给她的朋友们。

choices.text: Watch it with the man.
choices.zh: 和男士一起看它。

choices.text: Download and watch it.
choices.zh: 下载并观看它。

items.stem: What does the woman say about the comedy The Big Bang Theory?

choices.text: It has drawn criticisms from scientists.
choices.zh: 它遭到了科学家们的批评。

choices.text: It has been showing for over a decade.
choices.zh: 它已经播出了十多年。

choices.text: It is a ridiculous piece of satire.
choices.zh: 它是一部荒谬的讽刺作品。

choices.text: It is against common sense.
choices.zh: 它违背常识。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about players of contact sports?

choices.text: They are likely to get injured when moving too fast.
choices.zh: 他们在移动过快时很可能受伤。

choices.text: They believe in team spirit for good performance.
choices.zh: 他们相信团队精神能带来良好表现。

choices.text: They need to keep moving to avoid getting hurt.
choices.zh: 他们需要保持移动以避免受伤。

choices.text: They have to learn how to avoid body contact.
choices.zh: 他们必须学习如何避免身体接触。

items.stem: What do longevity statistics reveal about the average person?

choices.text: They do not have many years to live after retirement.
choices.zh: 他们退休后没有多少年可活。

choices.text: They tend to live a longer life with early retirement.
choices.zh: 他们往往因提早退休而活得更长。

choices.text: They do not start enjoying life until full retirement.
choices.zh: 他们直到完全退休才开始享受生活。

choices.text: They keep themselves busy even after retirement.
choices.zh: 他们即使退休后也让自己保持忙碌。

items.stem: What bonus does the "keep moving" principle bring us according to the speaker?

choices.text: It prevents us from worrying.
choices.zh: 它使我们免于担忧。

choices.text: It slows down our aging process.
choices.zh: 它减缓我们的衰老过程。

choices.text: It enables us to accomplish more in life.
choices.zh: 它使我们能够在人生中成就更多。

choices.text: It provides us with more chances to learn.
choices.zh: 它为我们提供更多学习机会。

items.stem: What does the passage say about people's mind?

choices.text: It tends to dwell upon their joyous experiences.
choices.zh: 它倾向于停留在他们快乐的经历上。

choices.text: It wanders for almost half of their waking time.
choices.zh: 它在他们醒着的时间里有近一半时间在游离。

choices.text: It has trouble concentrating after a brain injury.
choices.zh: 它在脑部受伤后难以集中注意力。

choices.text: It tends to be affected by their negative feelings.
choices.zh: 它往往会受到他们负面情绪的影响。

items.stem: For what purpose did the researchers develop the new app?

choices.text: To find how happiness relates to daydreaming.
choices.zh: 发现幸福感与白日梦的关系。

choices.text: To observe how one's mind affects one's behavior.
choices.zh: 观察一个人的思维如何影响其行为。

choices.text: To see why daydreaming impacts what one is doing.
choices.zh: 了解白日梦为何影响一个人正在做的事情。

choices.text: To study the relation between health and daydreaming.
choices.zh: 研究健康与白日梦之间的关系。

items.stem: How does daydreaming benefit people according to some researchers?

choices.text: It helps them make good decisions.
choices.zh: 它帮助他们做出正确的决定。

choices.text: It helps them tap their potentials.
choices.zh: 它帮助他们发掘自己的潜力。

choices.text: It contributes to their creativity.
choices.zh: 它有助于他们的创造力。

choices.text: It contributes to clear thinking
choices.zh: 它有助于清晰思考。

items.stem: What was the finding of the experiment with 145 undergraduates?

choices.text: Subjects with clear goals in mind outperformed those without clear goals.
choices.zh: 目标明确的受试者表现优于没有明确目标的受试者。

choices.text: The difference in performance between the two groups was insignificant.
choices.zh: 两组之间的表现差异不显著。

choices.text: Non-daydreamers were more focused on their tasks than daydreamers.
choices.zh: 非白日梦者比白日梦者更专注于他们的任务。

choices.text: Daydreamers did better than non-daydreamers in task performance.
choices.zh: 白日梦者在任务表现上优于非白日梦者。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about the Viking wooden churches?

choices.text: They are the oldest buildings in Europe.
choices.zh: 它们是欧洲最古老的建筑。

choices.text: They are part of the Christian tradition.
choices.zh: 它们是基督教传统的一部分。

choices.text: They are renovated to attract tourists.
choices.zh: 它们经过翻新以吸引游客。

choices.text: They are in worsening condition.
choices.zh: 它们的状况正在恶化。

items.stem: What is special about most of the Viking wooden churches?

choices.text: They have a history of 14 centuries.
choices.zh: 它们有14世纪的历史。

choices.text: They are 40 metres tall on average.
choices.zh: 它们平均高40米。

choices.text: They are without foundations.
choices.zh: 它们没有地基。

choices.text: They consist of several storeys.
choices.zh: 它们由多层构成。

items.stem: Why were the Viking churches constructed from wood?

choices.text: Wood was harmonious with nature.
choices.zh: 木材与自然和谐共处。

choices.text: Wooden buildings kept the cold out.
choices.zh: 木制建筑能够御寒。

choices.text: Timber was abundant in Scandinavia.
choices.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚木材资源丰富。

choices.text: The Vikings liked wooden structures.
choices.zh: 维京人喜欢木质结构。

items.stem: What are the three interesting studies about?

choices.text: Similarities between human babies and baby animals.
choices.zh: 人类婴儿与动物幼崽之间的相似之处。

choices.text: Cognitive features of different newly born mammals.
choices.zh: 不同新生哺乳动物的认知特征。

choices.text: Adults' influence on children.
choices.zh: 成人对儿童的影响。

choices.text: Abilities of human babies.
choices.zh: 人类婴儿的能力。

items.stem: What does the second study find about nine-month-old babies?

choices.text: They can distinguish a happy tune from a sad one.
choices.zh: 他们能够区分欢快的曲调和悲伤的曲调。

choices.text: They love happy melodies more than sad ones.
choices.zh: 他们更喜欢欢快的旋律而不是悲伤的旋律。

choices.text: They fall asleep easily while listening to music.
choices.zh: 他们在听音乐时很容易入睡。

choices.text: They are already sensitive to beats and rhythms.
choices.zh: 他们已经对节拍和节奏很敏感。

items.stem: What is the 1980 study about?

choices.text: Infants' facial expressions.
choices.zh: 婴儿的面部表情。

choices.text: Babies' emotions.
choices.zh: 婴儿的情绪。

choices.text: Babies' interaction with adult.
choices.zh: 婴儿与成人的互动。

choices.text: Infants' behaviors.
choices.zh: 婴儿的行为。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about being over collaborative?

choices.text: It may harm the culture of today's workplace.
choices.zh: 它可能损害当今职场的文化。

choices.text: It may hinder individual career advancement.
choices.zh: 它可能阻碍个人职业发展。

choices.text: It may result in unwillingness to take risks.
choices.zh: 它可能导致不愿承担风险。

choices.text: It may put too much pressure on team members.
choices.zh: 它可能给团队成员施加过大压力。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about people engaged in collaborative projects?

choices.text: They can hardly give expression to their original views.
choices.zh: 他们几乎无法表达自己的原创观点。

choices.text: They can become less motivated to do projects of their own.
choices.zh: 他们做自己项目的动力可能会降低。

choices.text: They may find it hard to get their contributions recognized.
choices.zh: 他们可能发现自己的贡献难以获得认可。

choices.text: They may eventually lose their confidence and creativity
choices.zh: 他们最终可能失去信心和创造力。

items.stem: How do people benefit from working in a team?

choices.text: They can enlarge their professional circle.
choices.zh: 他们可以扩大自己的职业圈子。

choices.text: They can get chances to engage in research.
choices.zh: 他们可以获得参与研究的机会。

choices.text: They can make the best use of their expertise.
choices.zh: 他们可以充分利用自己的专长。

choices.text: They can complete the project more easily.
choices.zh: 他们可以更轻松地完成项目。

items.stem: Why is it undesirable to spend too much time trying to reach consensus?

choices.text: It may cause lots of arguments in a team.
choices.zh: 它可能在团队中引发大量争论。

choices.text: It may prevent making a timely decision.
choices.zh: 它可能妨碍及时做出决策。

choices.text: It may give rise to a lot of unnecessary expenses.
choices.zh: 它可能产生大量不必要的开支。

choices.text: It may deprive a team of business opportunities.
choices.zh: 它可能剥夺团队的商业机会。
